question: JPMorgan Chase, Security Engineer (Java), Technical Interview 1. The coding task: **using Java Streams, merge two arrays keeping only the elements that are not common to both** (unique, non-common elements). The same round also covered Spring Boot annotations and bean lifecycle, `@Component` vs `@Bean`, REST API design and status codes, and tricky questions on concurrency and fail-fast vs fail-safe iterators.
lookingFor: Fluency with the Streams API (boxed, filter, concat, collect) rather than falling back to nested loops.
Choosing a hash set so membership checks are O(1) instead of O(n).
Handling edge cases: duplicates inside one array, empty arrays, null input.
Core Spring knowledge: annotations, lifecycle, `@Component` vs `@Bean`.
Understanding of collection iterator semantics under concurrent modification.
followUps: How would the solution change if the arrays are sorted or very large?
What happens if you remove from an ArrayList inside a for-each loop, and how do you do it safely?
How does Spring resolve which bean to inject when there are two candidates?
Why is `HashMap` not thread safe, and what do you use instead?
